# skilldrop

> 104 portable skills for the artifacts knowledge work ships (ADRs, design docs,
> PRDs, runbooks, threat models, decks, postmortems), plus 10 loops that sequence them
> behind gates. A loop orders skills; a skill never calls a skill, so every one of the
> 104 installs and runs alone by folder copy in Claude Code, Cursor, Kiro, Codex,
> Copilot and Antigravity. Zero runtime dependencies. This file indexes the docs so a tool
> can read the few relevant pages instead of the whole tree. Links are raw file content.
> Version 0.16.35.

## Start here

- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/README.md): what the project is, the role packs, and the one-command quick start.
- [guides/reference/skill-catalogue.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/reference/skill-catalogue.md): every skill, one line each, grouped by category.
- [guides/reference/loops.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/reference/loops.md): every loop's stages and gates.
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): the four primitives, the install contract, the enforcement model, the invariants. Read before proposing a structural change.
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/AGENTS.md): the canonical agent-context file — conventions, file placement, voice, and the pre-commit checklist.
- [guides/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/README.md): index of the long-form guides, split by Diátaxis kind.

## Loops — the operating model

Five loops cover the lifecycle and are separated by reversibility (how expensive the
mistake is to unwind), which is also what decides who may sign off. One wrapper applies
to any generator.

- [apply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/career/loops/apply/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: fit -> tailor -> letter -> form -> confirm. Gates: G6 (human), G6.1 (human).
- [build](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/dev-team/loops/build/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: shape -> implement -> verify -> decide. Gates: G2 (mechanical), G2.1 (human).
- [comply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/grc/loops/comply/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: register -> assess -> evidence -> check -> sign-off. Gates: G8 (mechanical), G8.1 (human).
- [design](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/solution-architect/loops/design/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: constrain -> shape -> threat -> ratify -> record. Gates: G1 (review).
- [discover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/product-manager/loops/discover/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: gather -> structure -> specify -> ratify. Gates: G0 (human).
- [measure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/data-analytics/loops/measure/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: spec -> review -> sign-off. Gates: G9 (review), G9.1 (human).
- [operate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/sre-oncall/loops/operate/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: instrument -> document -> respond -> learn. Gates: G4 (human).
- [release](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/dev-team/loops/release/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: plan -> ready -> announce -> go. Gates: G3 (review), G3.1 (human).
- [research](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/research/loops/research/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: plan -> synthesise -> compare. Gates: G7 (review).
- [ship-a-draft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/core/loops/ship-a-draft/LOOP.md) — *wrapper*, cap 3. Stages: intake -> draft -> critique -> polish. Gates: G5 (review).

## Machine-readable contracts

Closed schemas — an unknown key is a failure, not an extension point. Checked by a
stdlib JSON Schema subset in validate.py, never by a dependency.

- [contracts/agent.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/agent.schema.json): agents/<name>.md is a single markdown file whose YAML frontmatter is already Claude Code's format; the body is the system prompt.
- [contracts/catalogue.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/catalogue.schema.json): The catalogue index: pack display order, the outcome axis, and the skills that have left the catalogue.
- [contracts/guide.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/guide.schema.json): Diátaxis `kind` is a PAGE CONTRACT, not a directory requirement — the directory is a convenience, the frontmatter is the truth.
- [contracts/loop.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/loop.schema.json): A loop sequences existing skills; it never contains one.
- [contracts/pack.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/pack.schema.json): One pack's metadata.
- [contracts/policy.example.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/policy.example.json): 
- [contracts/policy.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/policy.schema.json): The file an organisation hands out (--policy, SKILLDROP_POLICY, or ~/.config/skilldrop/policy.json).
- [contracts/skill.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/skill.schema.json): This shape lived only as prose in AGENTS.md, so the one authoritative statement of what a manifest is was a paragraph a contributor had to read and obey.
- [contracts/terminals.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/terminals.json): the shared verdict vocabulary.

## Guides

- [Why loops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/explanation/loops.md) *(explanation)*: Why skilldrop sequences skills in a separate primitive instead of letting skills call each other, and why there are five lifecycle loops rather than three.
- [Operating model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/explanation/operating-model.md) *(explanation)*: Know which stage your work is in, which loop and pack help there, and where the agent stops for your decision.
- [Does the agent invent your resume?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/explanation/resume-fabrication-comparison.md) *(explanation)*: The same 14 resume and cover-letter requests run with the career pack's skills and with plain Claude Code - how often each put something in the document that the person never said, and what kind of thing it was.
- [What the benchmark showed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/explanation/what-the-benchmark-showed.md) *(explanation)*: Five days of measuring skills against the agent without them - a large gain on the skills' own checks, no blind preference at first, a gain that did not survive new evals, and what the skills that do win have in common.
- [Author a new loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/author-a-loop.md) *(how-to)*: How to add a loop — the closed loop.json contract, the three stage types, gate rules, and the checks that will reject a loop that only looks like governance.
- [Author a new skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/author-a-skill.md) *(how-to)*: The short version of the authoring path — what a skill must contain, what gates it, and where the full contributor rules live.
- [Benchmark skills against the agent without them](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/benchmark-skills.md) *(how-to)*: Run each acceptance eval twice as an agent session, with the skill and without it, and read the lift, the blind preference from two judges, and the cost.
- [Contain a skill's reach](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/contain-skills.md) *(how-to)*: Run a project's shell commands in Claude Code's sandbox, limited to the folder and the network hosts its skills declare, without loosening anything you already set
- [Roll out skilldrop across your org](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/enterprise-distribution.md) *(how-to)*: Bootstrap the hosted marketplace for every machine in one command — covers the public catalogue and private-fork setups for enterprise orgs.
- [Govern skills across an organisation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/govern-skills.md) *(how-to)*: Decide which catalogues and skills people may install, see what is installed on every machine, and keep a log of every change that shows if it was edited
- [Install a skill into your IDE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/install-per-ide.md) *(how-to)*: Put a skill where Claude Code, Cursor, Kiro, Codex, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot or another agent reads it, by copying the folder or with one CLI flag, then install its dependencies.
- [Install skills, packs and loops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/install.md) *(how-to)*: Install a role's pack, one skill, a loop or the reviewer subagents with the skilldrop CLI or the Claude Code plugin marketplace.
- [Use skilldrop with Figma](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/integrate-with-figma.md) *(how-to)*: Connect Figma files to the architecture and diagram skills — generate diagrams for FigJam, produce Figma-ready specs from a design session, or reverse-engineer decisions from a mockup.
- [Use skilldrop with GitHub Projects](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/integrate-with-github-projects.md) *(how-to)*: Pipe GitHub issues and project boards into skilldrop skills — implementation loops, review gates, and release notes that trace back to issues.
- [Use skilldrop with Jira](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/integrate-with-jira.md) *(how-to)*: Feed Jira tickets and epics into skilldrop skills — bug triage, story splitting, implementation loops, and release notes.
- [Use skilldrop with Linear](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/integrate-with-linear.md) *(how-to)*: Feed Linear issues, cycles, and projects into skilldrop skills for triage, story splitting, implementation tracking, and release notes.
- [Measure your loops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/measure-your-loops.md) *(how-to)*: Turn on the opt-in, local-only run log, then see which gates pass first time, which keep looping back, and which end in BLOCKED.
- [Use the AI engineering pack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/packs/use-the-ai-engineering-pack.md) *(how-to)*: Install the AI engineering pack, run its first task, and follow a typical session step by step.
- [Use the API builder pack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/packs/use-the-api-builder-pack.md) *(how-to)*: Install the API builder pack, run its first task, and follow a typical session step by step.

- [The skill contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/reference/skill-contract.md) *(reference)*: What a new skill folder must contain — frontmatter, manifest, size, scripts, evals, catalogue entries — and what validate.py checks before it merges.
- [Skills that ship scripts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/reference/skills-with-scripts.md) *(reference)*: Every skill that ships scripts and what each declares it needs — packages, environment variables, hosts, programs and files — and how to invoke a skill from Claude Code or any other IDE.
- [Updates and the install ledger](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/reference/update-and-ledger.md) *(reference)*: What outdated, update, diff and doctor compare and decide — the ledger file, how edited files become .upstream, every update flag, and the edge cases.
- [From use-case to deployed agent — the AI engineering workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/ai-engineering-workflow.md) *(tutorial)*: End-to-end AI adoption: triage the use case, assess org readiness, design the loop and agents, threat-model the system, build the evals, measure what shipped.
- [From complaint to closed incident](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/complaint-to-closed-incident.md) *(tutorial)*: A user complaint triggers a full response cycle — discover what's broken, operate to fix it, and close the loop with a postmortem and runbook update. Uses the discover and operate loops.
- [From a dashboard request to numbers people can defend](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/dashboard-request-to-defensible-numbers.md) *(tutorial)*: Run the measure loop on a real request. The spec cuts the charts that serve no decision, the SQL review catches a join that inflated revenue, and the loop stops for the metric owners instead of picking between two teams' definitions of an active customer.
- [From story to merged code — the dev-team workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/dev-team-workflow.md) *(tutorial)*: A complete dev-team session: split the story, implement with checkpoints, gate with the review panel, document what shipped.
- [Follow one change through the loops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/follow-a-change-through-the-loops.md) *(tutorial)*: A single realistic change — API rate limiting — walked from a stakeholder complaint to a closed incident, showing what each stage produces and what each gate actually refuses.
- [From idea to shipped feature](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/idea-to-shipped-feature.md) *(tutorial)*: A product idea moves through all five lifecycle loops — discover, design, build, release, operate — with each gate refusing until its conditions are met.
- [From a Terraform module to a plan you can safely apply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/module-to-safe-apply.md) *(tutorial)*: Write a reusable Terraform module with secure defaults, then review a plan that was meant to resize one app tier and would also have replaced a database, opened SSH to the internet and widened an IAM policy, with the infra-as-code pack.
- [One Markdown draft, every reader's format](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/one-draft-every-format.md) *(tutorial)*: Take one Markdown report to a Word file for the people who edit it, a spreadsheet for the people who total it, and one HTML file for everyone else, then bring a reply back to Markdown, with the converters pack. Nothing is dropped without being named.
- [From an unreadable page to a service people can use](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/page-to-service.md) *(tutorial)*: Rewrite a council permit page from what residents need, write every word on the application form, then blueprint the service behind it and find why two thirds of the calls are "where is my permit", with the experience-design pack.
- [From an agreed PRD to a tracker that stays honest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/prd-to-honest-tracker.md) *(tutorial)*: Load a PRD into Jira as epics and stories, triage the backlog it joins, write the weekly status from counted numbers, and catch where the tracker and the doc have drifted apart, with the trackers pack on one team's real files.
- [From signal to signed-off PRD — the product manager workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/product-manager-workflow.md) *(tutorial)*: A PM's full discovery-to-requirements session: sharpen the signal into a brief, test the narrative with a PR/FAQ, cascade OKRs, write the PRD, define metrics, critique before sharing.
- [From a risky change to a risk position its owner signs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/risky-change-to-signed-risk.md) *(tutorial)*: Run the comply loop on a payroll vendor move. The DPIA's risks to people join the register, two controls with no evidence lose the credit the ratings gave them, the register's own script decides G8, and the loop stops for the owner's signature.
- [From brief to committed design — the solution architect workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/solution-architect-workflow.md) *(tutorial)*: A full design session: capture the brief, draw the system, commit decisions as ADRs, write the design doc, threat-model it, gate with council review.
- [A why question to an answer the evidence carries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/why-question-to-evidence.md) *(tutorial)*: Run the research loop on a conversion drop everyone blames on a new onboarding flow. The plan fixes what would change the decision first, the gate refuses to pick between two tied explanations, and one reconciliation shows the drop was a tracking bug.
- [Write a skill your whole team can install, then review one before you trust it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/write-and-review-a-skill.md) *(tutorial)*: Turn a task you keep re-explaining to your agent into a portable skill folder with evals, then audit a teammate's skill that would have hidden where it saved files and run remote code, with the skill-engineering pack.

## Packs

Each skill and loop sits in exactly one pack folder, `packs/<pack>/`. Every role pack
except `api-builder` requires `core`, which installs with it.

- **core** (4 skills, loops: ship-a-draft): The cross-role toolkit every pack builds on: structured intake, document critique, the review council, and output hygiene, plus the ship-a-draft wrapper. Installed automatically with every role pack.
- **solution-architect** (10 skills, loops: design, requires core): Design-phase artifacts: diagrams, decision records, design docs, contracts, schemas, threat models, and the reviews that gate them.
- **product-manager** (9 skills, loops: discover, requires core): Direction to requirements: PR/FAQs, strategy frameworks, OKRs, business cases, interviews, PRDs, journey maps, and success measurement.
- **dev-team** (19 skills, loops: build, release, requires core): Build-and-ship: story splitting, implementation with adversarial review, test plans, triage, pull request descriptions, a ranked technical-debt register, migrations, launch readiness, release notes, agent-policy files, and code-quality gates.
- **sre-oncall** (7 skills, loops: operate, requires core): Operate the service: runbooks, observability design, incident communications, postmortems, and capacity/cost models.
- **stakeholder-comms** (4 skills, requires core): Non-technical audiences: audience profiling, exec summaries, decision logs, and guides. Decks live in the design pack.
- **design** (4 skills, requires core): On-brand visual work: capture a brand once, then build real PowerPoint decks and print-ready marketing flyers in that brand, with logo, colours and fonts applied.
- **ai-engineering** (12 skills, requires core): Adopt and build AI systems: readiness assessment, use-case triage, rollout and acceptable-use policy, plus agent loop design, subagent orchestration, spend budgets, agent security review, eval harnesses, and AI-usage reporting.
- **api-builder** (4 skills): Skills for teams building on the Anthropic API — prompt caching, token budgeting, eval generation for skills, and tool-use schema writing.
- **converters** (5 skills, requires core): Turn Markdown into Word, Excel and HTML files that people outside engineering can open, turn their files back into Markdown, and render diagrams to images. Standard-library Python scripts, with nothing to install.
- **experience-design** (5 skills, requires core): The experience around a product: the structure people navigate, the content and interface words they read, the components they use, and the service behind it all.
- **research** (3 skills, loops: research, requires core): Take a question from vague to answered: plan the research around the decision it serves, synthesise the sources with every claim cited, and rank rival explanations by the evidence against them.
- **trackers** (3 skills, requires core): For leads and PMs who run work in Jira, Linear or GitHub Projects: load a PRD into the tracker, triage the backlog, write the weekly status report, and check the tracker still matches the doc, all from an export or an MCP tool, with the numbers computed rather than estimated.
- **data-analytics** (2 skills, loops: measure, requires core): For analysts and the people who rely on their numbers: review SQL for the bugs that quietly inflate a figure, and spec dashboards around a decision instead of every chart that was easy to make.
- **grc** (4 skills, loops: comply, requires core): Governance, risk and compliance drafts for compliance leads, DPOs and risk owners: a risk register with a checked heat map, a GDPR data protection impact assessment, a SOC 2 control-to-evidence map, and answers to a customer security questionnaire drawn from your own evidence, each prepared for a qualified person to review.
- **infra-as-code** (2 skills, requires core): Terraform you can hand to another team and plans you can trust before apply: reusable modules with secure defaults, and a plan review that catches destroys, data loss, access widening and drift.
- **skill-engineering** (2 skills, requires core): For people writing Agent Skills in their own repos: write a portable SKILL.md folder from a described task, then audit any skill for routing, portability, safety, structure and evals before you share it.
- **career** (5 skills, loops: apply, requires core): Job applications, for any occupation: a shortlist of which of an employer's roles to go for, an honest check of your resume against the posting, a tailored resume and a cover letter that say nothing you didn't, the application form's answers drafted from your resume, and a script that lists every figure and name in a draft that your own resume doesn't contain.

## Outcomes — browse by why you are here

- **decide-what-to-build** (12 skills): Turn a direction into a committed, measurable plan: press releases, strategy frameworks, OKRs, business cases, requirements, PRDs, and the metrics that will say whether it worked.
- **design-the-system** (16 skills): Commit the shape before the code: decision records, design docs, diagrams, API and data contracts, migration and threat models, and the design of any agentic parts.
- **build-and-review-software** (19 skills): The loop around the code itself: supervised implementation, adversarial review panels, test plans, triage, pull request descriptions, a ranked technical-debt register, accessibility and static-analysis passes, and the policy files agents read.
- **build-on-the-claude-api** (4 skills): Skills for teams building directly on the Anthropic API — prompt caching strategy, token budgeting, eval generation, and tool-use schema writing.
- **run-and-recover-the-service** (10 skills): Operate what shipped: runbooks, observability design, release notes, incident communication, and the postmortem that closes the loop.
- **explain-it-to-decision-makers** (7 skills): Get a non-technical audience to a decision: audience profiling, deck outlines and real decks, exec summaries, decision logs, and how-to guides.
- **govern-ai-use** (6 skills): Adopt AI deliberately and prove what it is doing: readiness assessment, use-case triage, rollout plans, acceptable-use policy, adoption staging, and usage reporting.
- **create-on-brand-collateral** (4 skills): Make collateral that looks like it came from your team: capture the brand once, then build decks and print-ready flyers with your logo, colours and fonts.
- **get-a-draft-ready-to-ship** (8 skills): The passes either side of a generator: collect a messy input into a structured brief, critique the argument, and strip the machine artifacts before it leaves the building.
- **design-the-experience** (5 skills): Shape what people see and read before it's built: information architecture, interface copy, content specs, component specs and service blueprints.
- **research-a-question** (3 skills): Take a question to a sourced answer: a research plan with a stopping rule, a cited synthesis of the sources, and competing explanations weighed against the evidence.
- **define-and-trust-the-numbers** (2 skills): Make the numbers a business runs on mean one thing: SQL reviewed for wrong answers, and dashboards specced before they're built, with every number on them defined.
- **manage-risk-and-compliance** (4 skills): Prepare the material compliance asks for: a data protection impact assessment, a SOC 2 evidence map, a risk register with owners and review dates, and answers to a customer's security questionnaire with the evidence behind each.
- **build-agent-skills** (2 skills): Write and review Agent Skills for any tool: a portable SKILL.md with evals, and an audit of an existing skill before it ships.
- **apply-for-a-job** (5 skills): Choose which of an employer's roles to go for, then prepare one application that is tailored and true: an honest fit check against the posting, a resume reworked without adding a claim, a cover letter built only from what you supplied, and the application form's answers drafted from your resume.

## Reviewer subagents

- [code-quality](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/agents/code-quality.md): Craft-and-maintainability reviewer of just-written code. Finds what the next engineer will hate — bad names, tangled structure, duplication, needless complexity, leaky abstractions, dead code, and unreadable control flow. Does NOT hunt for bugs (that's the devils-advocate agent). Delegate to it when code works but you want it to read well before it ships.
- [devils-advocate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/agents/devils-advocate.md): Adversarial reviewer of just-written code and tests. Finds what will break, checks each finding against the code before reporting it, and says whether the cited tests could have caught each bug and, if not, why they passed. Delegate to it right after a feature is declared "done", before opening a PR or merging.
- [security-reviewer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/agents/security-reviewer.md): Security reviewer of just-written code and its dependencies. Hunts for exploitable weaknesses in the change — missing authz, injection, secret exposure, SSRF, unsafe deserialization, path traversal, weak crypto, and risky new dependencies. Does NOT hunt general bugs (that's devils-advocate) or model a design's threat surface (that's the threat-model skill). Delegate to it on a diff that touches auth, input handling, data access, external calls, or dependencies — before opening a PR or merging.

## The full catalogue

- [catalogue.json](https://sananthanarayan.github.io/skilldrop/catalogue.json): every skill, loop, pack and outcome as machine-readable JSON — name, description, tier, tags, related. Prefer this over scraping the site.
- [model-routing.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/model-routing.json): the abstract tier per skill (light/standard/heavy) and the provider map that resolves a tier to a concrete model.
- [catalogue.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/catalogue.json): pack display order and outcome membership; each pack's metadata is in `packs/<pack>/pack.json`.
- All 104 skills live at `packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; each has a `manifest.json` beside it. Fetch one directly: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
